findings.title: MCP API keys survive a password change
findings.description: The change signs out every other JWT session (per-user cutoff in the JWT branch of resolve_platform_user_unfloored) but the MCP-key branch never consults the cutoff and the change neither revokes nor lists the account's keys.
findings.exploit: Sign in with a leaked admin password; POST /api/mcp/keys (require_interactive, default scope user; ADMIN_GATE_SCOPES admits user) mints a key; the admin changes the password; the key keeps admin API access until revoked by hand.
findings.impact: The change does not evict an attacker who already minted a key, which is the threat #3825 exists for (#3799).
findings.recommendation: Surface the account's person-minted keys (user/ops/portal_delegate scopes, not agent/system/connector) in the change response and the panel, with an opt-in to revoke them in the same change.
findings.resolution: Opt-in revoke_api_keys on PUT /api/users/me/password revokes the caller's user/ops/portal_delegate keys; the response and panel report revoked/active counts. Tested incl. agent-key exclusion and a scope-filter mutation.
